lines.3: 「You've really got the perfect build for an easy delivery.」
lines.5: A sturdy body meant good health.
lines.6: And I had learned how precious that was.
lines.7: Kinu and I had been together ever since.
lines.8: After that much sex, of course we ended up with two kids.
lines.9: 「Now, let us speak with Date, who won the bronze medal in men's track and field.」
lines.11: 「Whoa. He really made something of himself.」
lines.12: Several athletes had withdrawn, and he'd had plenty of luck on his side.
lines.13: Even so, a Japanese athlete winning bronze in track was incredible.
lines.14: I hated that we hadn't been able to go cheer for him.
lines.15: 「It's been almost ten years. I bet Subaru doesn't even remember us anymore.」
lines.16: 「Well, track seems to be his entire life.」
lines.17: We hadn't spoken once since then.
lines.18: I'd tried contacting him several times, but never got through.
lines.19: And by the time I started working, my job and family--Kinu and the kids--kept my hands full.
lines.20: Before I knew it, Subaru had climbed all the way to those heights.
lines.21: It was unbelievable. My childhood friend was a bronze medalist.
lines.22: Then again, being friends with the head of Kiriya Company was already unbelievable enough.
lines.23: Erika Kiriya--the Princess--had seized control of Kiriya Company and now flew all over the world.
lines.24: I'd heard plenty about her ruthless methods, but that was the Princess for you.
lines.25: Yoshimi had taken a job at Kiriya Company.
lines.26: Apparently she stayed at the Princess's side, fretting over her tyrannical methods.
lines.27: I was sure she provided a great deal of emotional support too.
lines.28: Their friendship was still going strong.
lines.29: Otome was traveling the world with her grandfather, getting into street fights so she could eventually inherit the Kurogane dojo. (Training, in other words.)
lines.30: Even for training, that was an outrageous way to live...
lines.31: The Princess apparently wanted Otome to join Kiriya Company, but...
lines.32: As for Nagomi--it turned out she lived nearby.
lines.33: She was helping with her family's business.
lines.34: So she and Kinu were still friendly rivals who bickered constantly.
lines.35: She had always been pretty, but after turning twenty, she'd become so beautiful it was startling.
lines.36: But apparently her personality had kept every man away.
lines.37: ...Which felt like a bit of a waste.
lines.38: Fukahire worked at the post office.
lines.39: He liked having plenty of free time for his hobbies.
lines.40: Incidentally, he was still a virgin.
lines.41: He was working hard to win Nagomi over, but who knew how that would go? She didn't seem to give him the time of day.
lines.42: Ms. Inori was still working hard as a teacher.
lines.43: She had often been spotted strolling leisurely through town while already late.
lines.44: Rumor had it Yohei Murata and Noriko Nishizaki were dating.
lines.45: For all their fussing, those two suited each other.
lines.46: As for Subaru, the picture spoke for itself.
lines.47: He and the Princess were Ryuumeikan's twin sources of pride.
lines.48: 「You watching? I'm famous now. You really missed out when you didn't choose a great guy like me.」
lines.49: 「Hey, he's saying something that makes no sense.」
lines.50: 「He really is. What the hell is he saying on camera?」
lines.51: 「Wait. Was that a message for you?」
lines.53: I lost Subaru and gained Kinu.
lines.54: Subaru lost Kinu and gained a medal.
lines.55: ...You really couldn't have everything in this world.
lines.56: 「...And what will you do first when you return to Japan?」
lines.57: 「I'm going home. Time to return in glory.」
lines.60: 「You hear me, Leo, Kinu, Fukahire? Have the party ready.」
lines.62: 「That idiot... What is he doing on national television?」
lines.65: 「Even though he never contacted us once...」
lines.68: 「Still, you really did let an amazing man get away.」
lines.69: 「I don't regret it. I've always had eyes for you and nobody else.」
lines.73: 「Show him how much your cooking's improved--even if it's still too salty.」
